high.title: Korean Bonds Rally on WGBI Demand Hopes Despite KOSPI Surge - 3-Year Yield Down 5.2bp
high.summary: South Korean government bond yields fell broadly on July 31st, with the 3-year benchmark yield declining 5.2bp, driven by two converging catalysts. First, the government signaled its commitment to stabilizing long-term rates through its August treasury issuance plan released after the prior session's close — a direct signal of supply management intent that reassured duration buyers. Second, and more significantly, market participants positioned aggressively ahead of anticipated WGBI (World Government Bond Index) inclusion-related demand at month-end, creating a technical bid that overwhelmed even the dramatic equity surge (KOSPI up nearly 17% intraday, which would typically drive a risk-on rotation out of bonds).

high.title: Bank of Korea to Resume Gold Purchases After 13 Years – Secures Domestic Gold Procurement Channel
high.summary: The Bank of Korea (BOK) has announced it will purchase gold for the first time since 2013, establishing a formal cooperation framework with Korea Exchange, Korea Securities Depository, and domestic gold producer LS MnM. The BOK held a framework-signing event on July 20, 2026. Critically, the central bank will source **export-bound gold** to minimize domestic market disruption, and storage will be kept onshore. This is a meaningful strategic pivot in reserve management — the BOK's gold holdings as a share of total foreign exchange reserves have long been considered abnormally low relative to global peers. For KRW and bond traders, this signals a structural shift in how the BOK manages its reserve portfolio, with potential implications for USD reserve deployment. If gold purchases are funded by reducing USD-denominated assets, this could exert modest downward pressure on the BOK's USD holdings and influence KRW liquidity dynamics. Watch for the pace and scale of purchases in upcoming BOK reserve composition disclosures.

high.title: 'We Deliberated Extensively' – Why BOK Changed Its Mind on Gold Purchases After Years of Reluctance
high.summary: This analytical piece provides critical context behind the BOK's landmark decision to resume gold accumulation. According to market analysts cited in the article, the primary driver is **persistent geopolitical risk**, compounding a broader global trend of central banks diversifying away from dollar-denominated reserves. The BOK's gold allocation as a percentage of total FX reserves has been flagged as excessively low — well below the average of comparable central banks. The decision follows years of internal deliberation, suggesting this is a considered, strategic policy shift rather than a reactive move. For FX and rates traders, this has several implications: (1) It signals the BOK is actively reassessing reserve diversification, which could over time reduce marginal demand for US Treasuries; (2) It reinforces a cautious, risk-hedging posture by Korean monetary authorities amid elevated global uncertainty; (3) It may reflect subtle concerns about KRW reserve adequacy and geopolitical exposure. Market participants should monitor the **scale of planned purchases** and any follow-on communication from the BOK regarding reserve composition targets.

high.title: Dollar-Yen Extends Decline on U.S.-Japan Intervention Concerns
high.summary: The dollar-yen rate plunged sharply by 2.529 yen (1.589%) to 156.651 in New York trading, with the euro-yen similarly falling 1.77% to 180.310, as markets reacted to what appears to be coordinated U.S.-Japan currency intervention. This development carries significant implications for KRW dynamics. Historically, aggressive yen weakness has pressured Korean authorities to tolerate or even encourage KRW depreciation to maintain export competitiveness — particularly in autos and electronics where Japan and Korea directly compete. A sudden, intervention-driven yen reversal, however, could reduce that pressure and allow the BOK to hold a firmer KRW stance. For FX traders, the key watch point is whether this USD/JPY move is sustained or a temporary intervention-driven spike. If yen strength persists, expect reduced competitive devaluation pressure on KRW, potentially allowing for mild KRW appreciation. Korean equity investors should monitor export-sensitive sectors (autos, semiconductors) where a stronger yen is generally favorable for Korean competitiveness relative to Japanese peers.

high.title: US Treasuries Rally as Trump 'TACO' Backs Down on Iran Strike
high.summary: US Treasury prices rallied broadly after President Trump backed away from planned airstrikes on Iran, triggering a sharp drop in oil prices and a swift unwinding of inflation risk premiums in bond markets. The 10-year Treasury yield declined meaningfully as a result. This is directly relevant for Korean government bond (KTB) markets: a sustained US Treasury rally typically reduces upward pressure on KTB yields through global risk-off repricing and lower global inflation expectations. Lower oil prices also benefit Korea structurally as a major energy importer, easing domestic inflation pressures and giving the Bank of Korea greater flexibility on monetary policy. For KRW, the risk-off geopolitical retreat is mildly supportive — reduced global uncertainty tends to stabilize EM currencies. However, traders should watch whether the oil price decline sustains, as this would be the more durable driver for Korean inflation and BOK rate expectations. Watch KTB 3-year and 10-year yield spreads vs. UST for relative value signals.

high.title: Bank Household Loans Rise Over 4 Trillion Won for Second Straight Month on Mortgage, Credit Surge
high.summary: South Korean bank household loans expanded by more than 4 trillion won for the second consecutive month, driven by an 11-month high in mortgage loan growth and rising credit loans primarily through overdraft accounts, despite ongoing regulatory tightening measures by financial authorities. The persistence of household credit expansion despite total loan volume caps signals that regulatory tools are proving insufficient to meaningfully cool demand. This is a critical data point for BOK monetary policy deliberations: sustained household debt growth complicates the case for rate cuts, as easier financial conditions could further fuel leverage and housing market speculation. For KRW traders, elevated household debt constrains the BOK's easing cycle and may keep Korean short-end rates supported relative to market expectations. Bond investors should note that if this trend forces the BOK to maintain a hawkish hold or delay cuts further, the KTB curve could flatten as long-end yields respond to slower growth risks while short-end rates stay anchored. Watch for FSS (Financial Supervisory Service) and BOK commentary on macroprudential responses in coming weeks.

high.title: Dollar-Won Trades in Late 1,420s in New York Session
high.summary:
The USD/KRW exchange rate closed regular Seoul trading at 1,429.80, up 5.80 won from the prior session, before easing modestly to 1,428.00 during the New York overnight session (as of 8:40 PM KST). The 5.80-won intraday appreciation of the dollar signals continued selling pressure on the Won, keeping the pair firmly anchored in the upper 1,420s range. For KRW traders, the persistence above 1,425 is technically significant — a sustained break above 1,430 could invite further speculative dollar buying and potentially trigger Bank of Korea (BOK) verbal or direct FX intervention. The modest pullback in the New York session suggests some position squaring or overseas dollar selling, but the underlying bid for the dollar remains intact. Market participants should monitor whether the BOK steps in near the 1,430 level, which has historically acted as a psychological resistance point. The direction of global risk sentiment, U.S. Treasury yields, and any BOK commentary will be key near-term drivers for the pair. KRW-denominated bond investors should also watch for any spillover impact on foreign capital flows.

---

medium.title: President Lee to Hold Closed-Door Meeting on Real Estate and Stock Markets Upon Return
medium.summary:
President Lee Jae-myung is returning from an 11-day overseas tour (San Francisco and three South American countries) and will head directly to the Blue House to review domestic economic issues, specifically real estate market instability and sharp stock market fluctuations that persisted during his absence. Considerable controversy surrounding tax and capital market policies also arose during the trip. While this article does not directly address KRW/USD rates or BOK policy, the presidential focus on stock market volatility and capital market policy debate carries indirect relevance for Korean equity and FX traders. Any policy signals emerging from these closed-door meetings — particularly regarding capital gains tax or market stabilization measures — could influence KOSPI sentiment and short-term KRW flows. Investors should monitor post-briefing communications from the Blue House closely for any announcements on capital market reform or fiscal stimulus that may affect risk appetite and foreign capital positioning in Korean assets.

---

medium.title: [FX] Won Rebounds to Early 1,430s on Lack of Export Settlements, Bargain Buying
medium.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate partially reversed its prior overnight decline on July 31st, trading around 1,432.80 won as of 11:17 a.m. Seoul time — down 4.60 won from the previous close of 1,437.40 but well off the intraday low of 1,423.90 set at the open. The rebound was attributed to a notable absence of export settlement flows (Korean exporters converting USD earnings into KRW), which typically provide structural support for the won. Bargain buying of the dollar at lower levels also contributed to the recovery. The session's price action — a sharp gap lower open followed by gradual mean reversion — suggests the market tested KRW strength but lacked sufficient follow-through from domestic exporters to sustain it. **For FX traders:** The 1,420–1,425 zone is emerging as near-term support; a failure of exporters to sell into rallies keeps the won vulnerable to reversal. Watch for export settlement activity and any USD-supportive developments from the U.S. side.

medium.title: BOJ Holds Key Rate at 1%, Takata Dissents with Call for Hike
medium.summary: The Bank of Japan held its benchmark policy rate steady at 1.0% following its two-day meeting on July 31st, with the decision passing 8-1. The sole dissenter, board member Hajime Takata, advocated for an immediate hike to 1.25%, arguing the BOJ has entered a new policy phase requiring more proactive normalization. While a BOJ hold was consensus, the hawkish dissent is noteworthy for KRW traders given the JPY-KRW correlation and the competitive FX dynamics between the two currencies in Asian export markets. A more hawkish BOJ trajectory would support JPY strength, which historically exerts upward pressure on KRW as well, given Korea and Japan compete in similar export categories. **Watch:** Whether Takata's dissent signals a growing minority pushing for a September hike, which could meaningfully reprice JPY and ripple across Asian FX including KRW.

medium.title: Gundlach Says US Long-Term Rates Could Hit Mid-5% Range by Next FOMC
medium.summary: DoubleLine Capital CEO Jeffrey Gundlach projected in a CNBC interview that U.S. long-term interest rates could rise to the mid-5% range by the September FOMC meeting, even as the Fed held its funds rate at 3.50–3.75% at the prior meeting (with three dissents favoring cuts). If U.S. long-end yields surge toward 5%+, the rate differential pressure on KRW would intensify — potentially driving USD/KRW higher and complicating the BOK's policy calculus. Rising U.S. Treasury yields also pose headwinds for KTB demand from global investors, potentially offsetting some of the WGBI structural inflow story. **Watch:** U.S. 10-year Treasury yield trajectory into September as a key external risk variable for both KRW and Korean bond markets.

medium.title: Samsung Electronics Foreign Ownership Hits 16-Year Low – 'Underweighting Excessive'
medium.summary:
Samsung Electronics' foreign ownership ratio has dropped to its lowest level since 2010, a development with meaningful implications for KOSPI and capital flow dynamics. The widening — and now narrowing — gap between Samsung and TSMC in MSCI EM Index weightings has been a key driver of sustained foreign selling pressure on Korean equities. Securities firms are flagging the underweighting as excessive, suggesting potential for a positioning reversal if sentiment shifts. For KRW traders, prolonged foreign equity outflows are a structural headwind for the Won, as repatriation of equity proceeds by foreign investors adds selling pressure on KRW. A reversal in foreign ownership trends at Samsung could serve as an early signal of broader re-engagement with Korean risk assets, which would be constructive for KRW and KOSPI alike. Traders should monitor weekly foreign net buy/sell data on the Korea Exchange closely.

---

medium.title: Korea's July Exports Near $100 Billion, 2nd-Highest on Record; Chip Boom Powers Broad-Based Growth
medium.summary:
South Korea's exports approached $100 billion in July 2026, reaching the second-highest monthly export figure on record, driven by a historic semiconductor boom. This follows a record $87.75 billion print in May. Surging exports have direct relevance for KRW: robust export earnings generate strong USD inflows that typically support KRW appreciation, while also improving the current account surplus. For bond markets, strong trade data reduces the likelihood of emergency BOK easing, supporting a stable-to-higher yield environment. International fund managers should monitor whether this export strength translates into sustained current account surpluses in upcoming balance of payments data, which would be a structural positive for KRW.

---

medium.title: US July ISM Manufacturing PMI Hits 55.6 as Expansion Accelerates
medium.summary:
US manufacturing activity accelerated meaningfully in July, with the ISM PMI printing at 55.6 — well above the 50 expansion threshold — while the S&P Manufacturing PMI came in at 53.9, slightly above expectations. A stronger-than-expected US manufacturing recovery reinforces the narrative of resilient US growth, which typically supports a firmer USD and could limit near-term KRW upside. For Korean exporters, strong US demand is a positive demand signal, particularly for semiconductors and machinery. However, robust US activity data may also delay Federal Reserve rate cuts, keeping US-Korea rate differentials wide and maintaining pressure on KRW. Bond investors should monitor whether this data shifts Fed expectations, which would have direct knock-on effects on KTB yield spreads and foreign positioning in Korean fixed income.

---

medium.title: IRS Rates Fall on Middle East Negotiation Hopes, Strong Offers Concentrated in Short to Medium Terms
medium.summary: Korean Interest Rate Swap (IRS) rates declined across the curve on August 3rd, driven by rising expectations of U.S.-Iran diplomatic negotiations and a sharp drop in international oil prices. The 1-year IRS rate fell 2.25 basis points to 3.3900%, while the 3-year and 5-year tenors dropped 3.50bp and 2.25bp respectively, indicating stronger receiving interest in the belly of the curve. A market participant described flows as quiet with no significant directional conviction. For bond investors, the move reflects a mild risk-off/rates-down dynamic tied to easing geopolitical tension and lower oil, which could reduce inflation risk premium. The concentration of offer flow in short-to-medium terms suggests the market may be beginning to price in a more dovish BOK path or at minimum a plateau in policy rates. Traders should watch oil price stability and any BOK signaling for confirmation of a sustained rates decline.

medium.title: [Market Close] KOSPI Plunges 5.12% on Foreign and Institutional Selling — Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix Both Down 8%
medium.summary: The KOSPI reversed sharply lower, falling 5.12% to close at 6,257.45 — just one session after recording its largest-ever single-day gain of over 17%. The selloff was driven by heavy foreign and institutional selling, with anchor names Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each declining approximately 8%. While equities are not the primary focus for KRW and bond traders, the scale of foreign selling is directly relevant: sustained foreign equity outflows typically generate USD demand (KRW selling), adding upward pressure on USD/KRW and potentially weighing on Korean government bond demand from foreign holders. The extreme intraday volatility — a 17% surge followed by a 5% plunge in consecutive sessions — points to deeply uncertain market conditions. Fund managers should monitor foreign equity flow data closely as a leading indicator for KRW direction and capital account pressure.
